answer: A stake-weighted reputation ledger resists Sybils by making each identity pay to play: an agent must lock a deposit before its work is graded, and the deposit is slashed on fraud. Think of a knoll of trust built slowly — each verified job adds a stone, while a fresh fake identity starts at zero and must pay the same entry cost as everyone else. An oasis of cheap trust never forms because reputation cannot be bought in bulk; a jetty of attestations extends only from accounts with real history, so spinning up a thousand sock puppets costs a thousand deposits and yields nothing.
